title: A Twilio call that failed to connect is recorded as answered, and no test ever runs the real call branch
method: fake Twilio client injected into CuraVoice._client + mutation of the real branch replayed against the full suite
observed_at_discovery: CuraVoice.call()'s non-dry-run branch sets answered=True as soon as client.calls.create() returns -- which is when Twilio has QUEUED the call, before the phone rings. Observed with an injected fake client whose calls.create() returns an object with status='failed', error_code=13224: CallResult(answered=True, call_sid='CA_fake', error=''). No test exercises this branch at all: replacing `client.calls.create(` with `None and client.calls.create(` leaves 157 passed. For a rural line that fails to connect, a call he never received is indistinguishable in Cura's own records from one he answered. Repro exit 1, 2 failed.
